open_findings.detail: The code explicitly contains `model.addCons(start[u] >= start[v] + proc[v])` for the precedence pair (J1, J3). This enforces that J1 starts after J3 finishes, which is the exact opposite of the required constraint (J1 finishes before J3 starts). The logic is definitively reversed.

patch_commands: sed -i 's/model.addCons(start\[u\] >= start\[v\] + proc\[v\])/model.addCons(start[v] >= start[u] + proc[u])/' solve.py

reply.rationale: The precedence constraint was reversed: it enforced J1 starts after J3 finishes. The requirement is J1 completion <= J3 start, i.e. start[J3] >= start[J1] + proc[J1]. Swapping u/v fixes the direction while keeping all other logic (assignment, no-overlap disjunctions, objective) intact.
